candidate.title: Build break: `UsernameForm` calls the removed no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`
candidate.description: Commit `3214b188de` renamed `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` without updating the caller in the subclass. `UsernameForm.authenticate()` still invokes the zero-arg form; no zero-arg overload exists. Compilation fails: `method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types`. Fix: update call site to `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` or restore the zero-arg overload.

gold.title: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.f
gold.description: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

candidate.title: `user != null` in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` disables passkeys on anonymous login page
candidate.description: Adding `&& user != null` inverts conditional-UI passkey form from rendering in both first-login and re-authentication into re-auth only. At lines 115 and 137, `context.getUser()` is null on normal first login, so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` never runs and conditional-UI passkey autofill disappears. Contradicts tests asserting webauth form is present on initial anonymous login page. Fix: revert to `return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled();`.
